objectified_fact_types.description: The relationship 'Reviewer reviews Paper' is objectified as 'Review'. A Review is the concrete entity created when a reviewer reviews a paper, and the Review itself has properties (review score, review ID) and participates in other relationships. Rather than having reviewer and paper as separate attributes of Review, the objectification captures the act of reviewing as a first-class concept that can be identified, tracked, and given its own properties.

source_references.excerpt: each completed review gets its own review ID -- we treat the review itself as a thing we track... The review is the act of a particular reviewer reviewing a particular paper -- the score hangs off that pairing, not off the paper alone.

ambiguities.description: Relationship between 'Reviewer reviews Paper' and the objectified 'Review' entity. The transcript indicates that Review is the objectified version of the reviewer-paper relationship, but the model includes both the binary fact type 'Reviewer reviews Paper' (for cardinality specification) and two separate fact types 'Review is by Reviewer' and 'Review is for Paper' (for linking Review to its constituent entities). Clarification needed: Should 'Reviewer reviews Paper' be explicitly marked as the underlying relationship of the Review objectification, or should it be removed from the fact types since Review captures the relationship directly?

source_references.excerpt: Reviewers review papers. A reviewer can review many papers, and each paper gets several reviewers, but a given reviewer reviews a given paper at most once... The review is the act of a particular reviewer reviewing a particular paper -- the score hangs off that pairing, not off the paper alone.

ambiguities.description: Participation rules for Reviewer and Paper in the context of Review creation. The transcript establishes that every Review must have a Reviewer and a Paper, but does not clarify whether every Reviewer must perform at least one Review, or whether every Paper must be reviewed. Are these mandatory in the reverse direction?

source_references.excerpt: Reviewers review papers. A reviewer can review many papers, and each paper gets several reviewers... The review is the act of a particular reviewer reviewing a particular paper

ambiguities.description: Optionality of ReviewScore on Papers without Review. The constraint that 'a review without a score is not a review' establishes that individual Reviews always have scores. However, it is unclear whether a Paper can exist without any Review (and thus without any ReviewScore), or whether every Paper must have at least one Review with a score. The reverse direction of the 'Review has ReviewScore' fact type is not addressed.

source_references.excerpt: Every review has exactly one review score... A review without a score is not a review -- it always has exactly one.
